clue.text: Visionary quoted by a number in speech

indicators.note: in speech tells us the words are to be heard spoken, not read on the page

parts.note: quoted is CITED and a number is FOUR, the number going first, together said as one word

explanation.surface: A prophet is cited by a crowd of people in conversation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' here means beside, so the number FOUR stands next to CITED, and FOUR CITED is how the word sounds aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone able to see what lies ahead, a visionary, is described as having foresight.

clue.text: American cop given sustenance

definitions.meaning: US slang for an FBI agent, a federal officer
past participle of the verb to feed, meaning nourished

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: US slang for a federal agent, and the past tense of feed, meaning nourished.

clue.text: Twickenham players have the stomach for it?

parts.note: Twickenham is the home of English rugby union (RU), whose players are men
Twickenham is the home of English rugby union (RU), whose players are men

explanation.surface: Asking whether rugby players at their home ground are keen on the game.
explanation.walkthrough: Twickenham is the London stadium of English rugby union, abbreviated RU. 'stomach for it' reads as appetite, but stomach is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The rumen is the first stomach chamber of a cow or other ruminant animal.

clue.text: Workers going about distributing news mag

indicators.note: distributing spreads the letters of news mag around into a new order

explanation.surface: A newsagent's staff go on their rounds handing out a news magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distributing' fits the surface of delivering magazines but scrambles the letters of NEWS MAG. Swagmen are Australian itinerant workers carrying their swag.
explanation.definitionFit: Swagmen were itinerant Australian labourers tramping the country carrying their belongings.

clue.text: Former statesman's ways of proceeding against outlaw, mostly

parts.note: gaits are manners of walking or moving along

indicators.note: mostly means the word is shortened by its final letter

parts.note: Ned Kelly was the famous Australian bushranger outlaw

explanation.surface: An ex-politician's methods ran up against a criminal, more or less.
explanation.walkthrough: 'against' means next to, joining the pieces; the 's of statesman's stands for 'is'. Hugh Gaitskell led the British Labour Party from 1955 to 1963.
explanation.definitionFit: Hugh Gaitskell was a British Chancellor and Labour leader, a statesman now dead.

clue.text: Light vehicle in India and part of Polynesia

definitions.meaning: a light two-wheeled horse-drawn cart used in India
a South Pacific island kingdom in Polynesia

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: an Indian horse-drawn cart, and the Polynesian island kingdom of the South Pacific.

clue.text: Wanted knight to take part in action

indicators.note: to take part in puts the knight within the action, one piece placed inside another

parts.note: a deed is an action
Sir is the title of a knight

explanation.surface: A knight was keen to join the battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to take part in' suggests a knight joining a fight, but it is the container signal, putting the title inside the action.
explanation.definitionFit: Desired and wanted are synonyms, both meaning longed for.

clue.text: Giant bird: I don't believe it will be repulsed

indicators.note: repulsed means driven back, so the exclamation is turned round

parts.note: Cor! is a British exclamation of surprise or disbelief

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to believe a huge bird can be beaten off.
explanation.walkthrough: COR is British slang for an exclamation of amazement. The roc is the huge bird of the Arabian Nights.
explanation.definitionFit: The roc is a mythical enormous bird of prey from Arabian legend.

clue.text: Look again at compensation a daughter's received

indicators.note: received means the compensation takes the other letters inside itself

parts.note: redress is compensation for a wrong
D is the abbreviation for daughter; the 's stands for has

explanation.surface: A daughter has been paid damages and reconsiders the case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'received' puts A and D inside REDRESS, after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To readdress an issue is to tackle or consider it once more.

clue.text: After change of head, teacher put study first, I guess

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart

indicators.note: change of head means the opening letter of the teacher is swapped for another

parts.note: a lecturer is a university teacher

explanation.surface: A teacher, after a change of headmaster, puts study first and speculates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After change of head' swaps the teacher's first letter for J; 'put study first' simply sets the study word ahead of it.
explanation.definitionFit: A conjecturer is someone who guesses, so 'I guess' describes that speaker in the role.

clue.text: Cursing mother country

parts.note: a dam is the mother of an animal
a nation is a country

explanation.surface: Swearing at the motherland.
explanation.definitionFit: Damnation can be an act of cursing, or an oath uttered as a curse.

clue.text: Pen name, one of Proust's?

parts.note: a pen is a female swan

explanation.surface: Asking whether a pen name belongs to Proust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pen name' looks like a pseudonym, but Pen is a female swan. Swann is the title character of Proust's 'Swann's Way'.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Swann is a principal character in Proust's novel cycle, so he is one of Proust's people.

clue.text: Note American name for youngest son?

parts.note: a minim is a musical note, a half note

explanation.surface: A remark about what Americans call their youngest boy.
explanation.walkthrough: At British public schools, the youngest of brothers with the same surname was called Minimus (after Major and Minor).
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for least, used in English boarding schools to label the youngest of several brothers.

clue.text: Going round ship, sailor assembles garments for officers

indicators.note: going round tells us the gathering word encircles the ship and sailor

parts.note: meets means gathers together
SS is the abbreviation for steamship
Jack, as in Jack Tar, is a sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor making his way round the ship collects uniforms for the officers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going round' reads like a sailor touring the ship, but it means the gathering word wraps round ship and sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: Mess jackets are short formal jackets worn by officers at dinner in the mess.

clue.text: A game in which players bid to make contract

parts.note: in the card game bridge the players bid for a contract

explanation.surface: In contract bridge, players bid to win their contract.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contract' reads as the bridge term for the bid, but it is a verb meaning shrink.
explanation.definitionFit: To abridge is to shorten, which is to make something contract.

clue.text: Girl with blooming black eye?

parts.note: a girl's name that, with black-eyed before it, names a flowering plant, so blooming means in flower, not bruised

explanation.walkthrough: The black-eyed Susan is a yellow daisy-like garden flower with a dark centre.
explanation.definitionFit: A common girl's name that is also part of the flower name black-eyed Susan.

clue.text: Turn strumpet into wise maiden? That's the plan

indicators.note: into puts the reversed woman inside the wise word

parts.note: sage means wise

indicators.note: turn means the word for the strumpet is read backwards

parts.note: a tart is slang for a strumpet
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A scheme to reform a prostitute into a sensible young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn' reverses the strumpet word, and 'into' sets that inside the wise word after its first letter; the cricket maiden follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A stratagem is a scheme or plan, often a clever one devised to outwit someone.

clue.text: Convenient means to remove marks from old part of Parthenon?

parts.note: ex means former

indicators.note: to remove asks for the marks to be taken out of the temple part

parts.note: a pediment is the triangular gable of a classical temple such as the Parthenon
M was the abbreviation for the German mark currency

explanation.surface: A handy way to clean graffiti off an old section of an ancient Greek temple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'marks' surfaces as stains but is M, the old German currency.
explanation.definitionFit: An expedient is a handy means to an end, something convenient though perhaps not principled.

clue.text: Briefly spot bird lurking inside garden plant

indicators.note: lurking inside puts the bird within the shortened spot
briefly means the spot word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: a pimple is a spot on the skin
the erne is the sea eagle, a crossword favourite

explanation.surface: A small spot reveals a bird hiding among the flowers in the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Briefly' drops the spot's last letter, and 'lurking inside' sets the sea eagle within what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: The scarlet pimpernel is a small red-flowered plant found in gardens and fields.

clue.text: Judge left to probe piece of legislation about disputed city

indicators.note: to probe means the left letter pushes its way into the legislation
about means the legislation is turned round to read backwards

parts.note: a measure is a proposed law or piece of legislation

explanation.surface: A judge has been left to investigate a law concerning a contested city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses the legislation to ERUSAEM, and 'to probe' sends the left letter into it near the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Jerusalem is claimed as capital by both Israelis and Palestinians, so its status is disputed.

clue.text: Bird and fish fed to pig

indicators.note: fed to means the fish is put into the pig, as food goes inside

parts.note: a sow is a female pig
a parr is a young salmon

explanation.surface: A bird and some fish are given to a pig as feed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bird and fish' looks like a list of two answers; only Bird defines, and 'fed to' puts the young salmon inside the pig.
explanation.definitionFit: A sparrow is a small brown songbird.

clue.text: Problem, loosening ropes

indicators.note: loosening the ropes lets their letters fall into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Untying knotted ropes is a tricky task.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loosening' rearranges the letters of ROPES.
explanation.definitionFit: A poser is a puzzling question or difficult problem.

clue.text: Top receptionist keeps order

indicators.note: keeps means the two words hold the answer within their letters

explanation.surface: The senior receptionist maintains order in the office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeps' tells you the answer sits inside 'Top receptionist', spanning the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: A precept is a rule or command, an order to guide conduct.

clue.text: Mocking remark about lines at end of act being fluffed

indicators.note: at end of puts about and lines after the jumbled act
an act being fluffed is botched, so its letters are mixed up

parts.note: CA, for circa, means about

explanation.surface: Jeering at the actors' lines when the end of the performance is bungled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being fluffed' turns ACT into CAT; CA and LL go 'at end of' it.
explanation.definitionFit: A catcall is a shrill whistle or jeer, a derisive remark at a performer.

clue.text: Keeps on losing hat in strong gusts of wind

indicators.note: losing hat means the word loses its top letter, the first one

parts.note: blasts are strong gusts of wind

explanation.surface: Someone keeps losing their hat in high winds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing hat' removes the B at the head of BLASTS.
explanation.definitionFit: To last is to continue or endure, so lasts means keeps on going.

clue.text: Jumper always has hole in it

indicators.note: has with in it means the poetic word holds the other inside
in it means the hole sits within the word for always

parts.note: e'er is the poetic contraction of ever, meaning always
a vent is a hole or opening

explanation.surface: A sweater that always has a hole in it.
explanation.walkthrough: The poetic contraction of ever is used for always. 'Jumper' suggests a sweater but means a horse or rider in eventing; 'has' and 'in it' signal the container.
explanation.definitionFit: An eventer is a horse or rider in eventing, which includes show jumping and cross-country.

clue.text: Times team deleting article on page one

indicators.note: deleting means the article is cut from the team

parts.note: taken from the clue's word team
a is the indefinite article
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A newspaper's team strike out an article on the front page.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' suggests the newspaper, but it is plural of tempo, a musical speed.
explanation.definitionFit: Tempi is the plural of tempo, the speed or time at which music is played.

clue.text: Retro jazz piece by the French composer

indicators.note: retro means backwards, so the jazz piece and the French word are read in reverse

parts.note: a rag is a piece of ragtime music
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A nostalgic jazz tune by a French composer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retro' turns the jazz piece and the French article round together. Edward Elgar wrote the 'Enigma Variations'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Edward Elgar was an English composer, known for the Pomp and Circumstance marches.

clue.text: Cover arranged to protect peacekeepers at the front

indicators.note: to protect means the arranged word wraps round the others as a shield

parts.note: set means arranged
UN, the United Nations, supplies peacekeeping forces
the helm is where a vessel is steered, taken as its front position

explanation.surface: Body armour is organised to shield UN troops in the front line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to protect' makes the arranged word wrap round the peacekeepers and the front-of-ship word, after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A sun helmet, or pith helmet, is a light hat worn as a cover against tropical sun.

clue.text: Cask is exported from North African city

indicators.note: exported from means is goes out of the city

parts.note: Tunis is the capital of Tunisia

explanation.surface: A barrel is shipped out from a North African port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is exported from' sounds like trade, but IS is taken out of TUNIS.
explanation.definitionFit: A tun is a large cask for wine or beer.

clue.text: Money essential if finishing early and retiring?

indicators.note: retiring means withdrawing, so the shortened word is read backwards
finishing early means the word stops before its final letter

parts.note: a must is an essential

explanation.surface: Asking whether cash is vital if one quits work early and retires.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finishing early' cuts MUST to MUS, and 'retiring' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A sum is an amount of money.

clue.text: Leith's a town that developed in a Scottish county once

indicators.note: developed means the letters are built up into a new shape

parts.note: the letters of Leith with its s

explanation.surface: Leith is a town that grew up in a former Scottish county.
explanation.walkthrough: 'developed' rearranges the three words before it. Leith is Edinburgh's port; West Lothian was a Scottish county before the 1975 reorganisation.
explanation.definitionFit: West Lothian was a historic county of Scotland, abolished as such in 1975.
